newsitem.title: UK: Euro stocks firm but Greenspan nerves emerge.
newsitem.headline: Euro stocks firm but Greenspan nerves emerge.

text.p: European stocks were strong on Tuesday but London slipped towards the close due to a weaker Wall Street and jitters about what U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan will tell Congress this week.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar recovered a little after easing from early highs against the mark, with the market short of stimuli before Greenspan delivers his report on the U.S. economy on Wednesday.

French and German stocks led the way with both markets up about 1.55 percent, even though Wall Street got off to a slow start as Greenspan caution pushed the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 23.86 points to 6,984.34 by late morning.
In Frankfurt, the DAX Index closed up 49.0 points at 3,233.21 while the Paris CAC-40 index finished 39.87 higher at 2,607.72.

Dealers said the continental European markets were reacting not to Tuesday's Dow but its Monday perfomance when it jumped 1.1 percent to 7,008.20 due to a strong U.S. economy, a firm dollar and low inflation.
"This is really the follow-through from Wall Street yesterday," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The Street isn't really doing that much today, but a lot of stocks seem better on sentiment."

London was more susceptible to Wall Street and the FTSE 100 index fell from a high of 4,357.9 -- less than five points below the record -- to close up a more modest 0.3 percent or 13.6 points at 4,344.7.

Early in the day, European investors seemed to have set aside their traditional wariness before the Fed chairman Greenspan speaks. But later the tide of opinion began to turn as thoughts focused on his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress.
Last autumn Greenspan caught investors off guard when he wiped billions of dollars off share prices worldwide by warning them of "irrational exuberance" on the markets.
Since then, he has delivered a gentler assessment of the markets, and interest rates have remained stable as the U.S. economy has achieved steady growth with low inflation.

Analysts expect him to give a positive report when he testifies to the Senate Banking Committee at 1500 GMT on Wednesday and to a House Banking subcommittee on March 5. But he may include some words of caution about the course of inflation and possibly the stock market.
The dollar was at 1.6774 marks, off the day's low and above its late European level of 1.6700 on Monday. Against the yen, it also reversed earlier slippage to 122.05, unchanged from late on Monday.
Some analysts said the dollar's energy was flagging, but this suggested the market was waiting for cues on which way to go, and the slowness did not necessarily herald a downturn.

"In general we need more information, either to confirm a dollar topping scenario or to send the dollar up against the mark and yen," said Teis Knuthsen, international economist at First Chicago in London.

Tuesday's crop of U.S. data had little effect. A confidence index slipped in February but was still above forecast. U.S. import prices dropped 0.3 percent in January after a rise of 0.1 percent in December, while export prices were up 0.2 percent after being flat in the previous month.
Elsewhere, the Italian government won a parliamentary confidence vote as expected but the lira still fell to 995.30 to the mark from 992.55 at the opening.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted at 1.6774 marks and 122.05 yen, compared with 1.6700 and 122.05 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 13.6 points at 4,344.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 39.87 points to 2,607.72.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 49.0 points at 3,233.21. The electronic IBIS index was up 52.71 at 3,233.34.
PRECIOUS METALS AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
Gold closed at $353.65 an ounce after an afternoon fixing at $353.10 and a $353.45 morning fix. Silver was down one cent at $5.21.
